In mathematics, a '''corestriction'''<ref name=dh68>{{cite book
 | last1 = Dauns | first1 = John
 | last2 = Hofmann | first2 = Karl Heinrich
 | mr = 247487
 | page = ix
 | publisher = American Mathematical Society
 | series = Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society
 | title = Representation of rings by sections
 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=4sPTCQAAQBAJ&pg=PR9
 | volume = 83
 | year = 1968| isbn = 978-0-8218-1283-9
 }}</ref> of a function is a notion analogous to the notion of a [[restriction (mathematics)|restriction]] of a function. The duality prefix co- here denotes that while the restriction changes the [[domain of a function|domain]] to a [[subset]], the corestriction changes the [[codomain]] to a subset. However, the notions are not [[Dual (category theory)|categorically dual]].

Given any subset <math>S\subset A,</math> we can consider the corresponding [[Inclusion map|inclusion]] of sets <math>i_S:S\hookrightarrow A</math> as a function. Then for any function <math>f:A\to B</math>, the [[Restriction (mathematics)|restriction]] <math>f|_S:S\to B</math> of a function <math>f</math> onto <math>S</math> can be defined as the [[function composition|composition]] <math>f|_S = f\circ i_S</math>.

Analogously, for an inclusion <math>i_T:T\hookrightarrow B</math> the corestriction <math>f|^T:A\to T</math> of <math>f</math> onto <math>T</math> is the unique
function <math>f|^T</math> such that there is a [[functional decomposition|decomposition]] <math>f = i_T\circ f|^T</math>. The corestriction exists if and only if <math>T</math> contains the [[image (mathematics)|image]] of <math>f</math>. In particular, the corestriction onto the image always exists and it is sometimes simply called the corestriction of <math>f</math>. More generally, one can consider corestriction of a morphism in general [[Category theory|categories]] with images.<ref>nlab, Image, https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/image</ref> The term is well known in [[category theory]], while rarely used in print.<ref>(Definition 3.1 and Remarks 3.2) in Gabriella Böhm, Hopf algebroids, in Handbook of Algebra (2008) arXiv:0805.3806</ref>

Andreotti<ref>paragraph 2-14 at page 14 of Andreotti, A., Généralités sur les categories abéliennes (suite) Séminaire A. Grothendieck, Tome 1 (1957) Exposé no. 2, http://www.numdam.org/item/SG_1957__1__A2_0</ref> introduces the above notion under the name {{lang|fr|coastriction}}, while the name corestriction reserves to the notion categorically dual to the notion of a restriction. Namely, if <math>p^U:B\to U</math> is a [[surjective function|surjection]] of sets (that is a [[quotient space (topology)|quotient map]]) then Andreotti considers the composition <math>p^U\circ f:A\to U</math>, which surely always exists.
